title: 1996 AHSME Problem 17
statement: In rectangle \(ABCD,\) angle \(C\) is trisected by \(\overline{CF}\) and \(\overline{CE},\) where \(E\) is on \(\overline{AB},\) \(F\) is on \(\overline{AD},\) \(BE=6,\) and \(AF=2.\) Which of the following is closest to the area of the rectangle \(ABCD?\)

solutions.text: Let the rectangle have width \(w\) and height \(h.\) In right triangle \(CBE,\) \(\tan30^\circ=\frac{BE}{CB}=\frac{6}{h},\) so \(h=6\sqrt3.\) In the triangle using \(C,F,D,\) the horizontal run is \(w\) and the vertical drop is \(h-2,\) so \(\tan60^\circ=\frac{w}{h-2}.\) Hence \[ w=\sqrt3(6\sqrt3-2)=18-2\sqrt3. \] The area is \(6\sqrt3(18-2\sqrt3)\) \(=108\sqrt3-36\approx151.1,\) closest to \(150.\) Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Each of the three angles at \(C\) is \(30^\circ\)
Use the two right triangles adjacent to sides \(CB\) and \(CD\) to determine the rectangle’s height and width
